messages:
sanjay: Heads up — CI CodeQL job for the scan-agent service account started failing right after the RBAC prune this morning. Seeing KMS decrypt permission errors in the job log.

sanjay: Log snippet:
```
ERROR: failed to access secret: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = cryptoKeyVersions/decrypt denied for serviceAccount:scan-agent@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
stack: github.com/redwood/infra/pkg/kms.Decrypt
```

maria: ugh. which PR did the prune come from? sounds like we removed a roleBinding.

sanjay: PR #4827 (iam-cleanup). @izzy do you remember which bindings we removed from scan-agent?

izzy: yep that PR removed an old broad role. We left the minimal project.viewer but removed a handful of service-specific roles. I suspected scan-agent was overprivileged; didn't realize it used KMS.

devops-oncall: quick mitigation: re-grant the least-privilege key access for the scan-agent to unblock CI, then we can tighten. Would prefer a short-lived roleBinding so we don't reintroduce permanent overprivilege. :+1:

maria: agree. also want to confirm audit logs capture who invoked decrypts — we need that for compliance ticket. Are audit logs enabled and forwarded to Splunk?

izzy: yes, project-level audit logging for DATA_ACCESS is on. Splunk ingestion still good — forwarded to index "sec-audit". But note: we only log the KMS CryptoKey request metadata; we don't log plain secrets.

secbot: New triage created: VULN-2026-023 (CI failure due to KMS permission). Assigned to izzy, severity: P2. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/crypto-kms-audit

izzy: proposed short-term fix (apply immediately):
```bash
# grant decrypt on key to service account
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ci-keys/cryptoKeys/scan-secrets \
  --member="serviceAccount:scan-agent@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"
```
After that, restart the CI runner.

maria: can you also add a conditional audit entry so we can see which workflows hit the key? I want a Splunk dashboard tile for that.

izzy: will add an explicit log sink filter for audit logs and tag the workflow name in the log parsing rules. tiny followup: the scan-agent also writes an upload to the internal artifact bucket — that path is covered by the existing data-access logs.

sanjay: small security note: while re-granting, let's not add broad roles like "editor" or project-level owner. only the cryptoKeyDecrypter scope.

devops-oncall: also adding a temporary canary alert: if more than 3 decrypt failures of the same service account within 5m, open pager. saves debugging loops.

izzy: +1. I'll push the IAM change and the alert. after we confirm CI green, I'll open a follow-up to add least-privileged key-level IAM managed by terraform and mark the stale binding removal in the PR description.

maria: separate item — the CodeQL run flagged a couple of low-confidence SAST issues (unsafe regex & potential path join). I reviewed; looks like false positives for our scanner harness. Will mark as "noise" with evidence and add suppression comment per the SAST policy.

secbot: SAST finding VULN-2026-024 created and linked to thread 1812345678. Tagging reviewers: @maria, @sanjay.

sanjay: thanks. once izzy confirms patch + CI green, please paste the terraform diff so security can review the exact binding. Also ensure audit retention is 90d for key access events.

izzy: will do. ETA ~25m to apply binding and rerun CI. Posting the terraform snippet after apply for review.

maria: sounds good. assign me on the follow-up ticket for the SAST suppression evidence and the Splunk dashboard item.

devops-oncall: noted. I'm toggling the temporary pager and will revert after confirmation.

sanjay: thanks team. keep updates brief here. :thumbsup:
